hook.line: A road is closed and Tomás has to cross Bogotá for a delivery. Everyone he meets has an opinion on the best way round, and the words they use are worth having.
hook.es: Dimos un rodeo para evitar el trancón.
hook.en: We took a detour to avoid the traffic jam.

examples.es: Dimos un rodeo para evitar el trancón.
examples.en: We took a detour to avoid the traffic jam.

examples.es: Tomé un atajo por el parque.
examples.en: I took a shortcut through the park.

examples.es: Agarramos un atajo y llegamos antes.
examples.en: We took a shortcut and got there earlier.

examples.es: Don Hernando dio un rodeo por la Séptima.
examples.en: Don Hernando took a detour along the Séptima.

examples.es: Mariana le dijo la verdad a Tomás sin rodeos.
examples.en: Mariana told Tomás the truth without beating around the bush.

rule:
Two ways to get somewhere:

*Dar un rodeo* = take the long way round, a detour. *Dimos un rodeo.*

*Tomar un atajo* or *agarrar un atajo* = take a shortcut. In Latin America, *agarrar* is very common here. Never *coger*.

*Rodeo* works for talking too. *Sin rodeos* = "straight out". *Dar rodeos* = to beat around the bush.

English says "take" for both. Spanish uses *dar* for the detour and *tomar* or *agarrar* for the shortcut.
smallPrint: Teachers call these collocations: words that natives expect side by side, so you learn them as a pair.

readAndPick.es: Dimos un rodeo para evitar el trancón.
options: We took a shortcut to the traffic jam.
We took a detour to avoid the traffic jam.
We got stuck in the traffic jam.

readAndPick.es: Tomé un atajo por el parque.
options: I took a shortcut through the park.
I took the long way round the park.
I walked in the park all day.

readAndPick.es: Agarramos un atajo y llegamos antes.
options: We took a detour and got there later.
We took a shortcut and got there earlier.
We took a shortcut and got lost.
Speak slowly, please.
Speak plainly, please.
Don't speak at all, please.

readAndPick.es: Mariana le dijo la verdad a Tomás sin rodeos.
options: Mariana told Tomás the truth bluntly.
Mariana walked around Tomás to tell him the truth.
Mariana told Tomás a lie.

readAndPick.es: Tuvimos que dar un rodeo porque cerraron la calle.
options: We took a shortcut because the street was closed.
We had to take a detour because the street was closed.
We closed the street ourselves.

readAndPick.es: No des tantos rodeos y dime qué pasa.
options: Don't take so many shortcuts and tell me what's up.
Take as many detours as you want.
Stop beating around the bush and tell me what's going on.

readAndPick.es: Es mejor dar un rodeo que llegar tarde por el trancón.
options: It's better to take a detour than to be late because of the jam.
It's better to take a shortcut than to be late because of the jam.
It's better to wait in the jam than to take a detour.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *dar* or *tomar*: Dimos ___ rodeo para evitar el trancón. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Dimos un rodeo para evitar el trancón.
yourTurn.why: The long way round is *dar un rodeo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *rodeo* or *atajo*: Tomé un ___ por el parque. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Tomé un atajo por el parque.
yourTurn.why: A shortcut is *un atajo*, and the verb is *tomar* or *agarrar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "We took a shortcut and got there earlier."
yourTurn.answer: Agarramos un atajo y llegamos antes.
accept: Tomamos un atajo y llegamos antes.
yourTurn.why: *Agarrar un atajo* is the everyday way to say it.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "Speak plainly, please." (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Sin rodeos* means with no detours, straight to the point.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "Don Hernando took a detour along the Séptima."
yourTurn.answer: Don Hernando dio un rodeo por la Séptima.
yourTurn.why: The long way is *dar un rodeo*, and *dio* matches one person in the past.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "We had to take a detour because they closed the street."
yourTurn.answer: Tuvimos que dar un rodeo porque cerraron la calle.
yourTurn.why: *Tener que* + *dar un rodeo* gives "had to take a detour".

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a command to a friend: *Das tantos rodeos.* Say "Don't take so many detours."

pitfalls.wrong: Tomamos un rodeo para evitar el trancón.
pitfalls.right: Dimos un rodeo para evitar el trancón.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A detour goes with *dar*, a shortcut with *tomar* or *agarrar*.
Almost. You do not "give" a shortcut; you take it.
Almost. To mean "plainly" you need *sin*, with no detours.

personal: Describe how you get to work, school or the shop. Is there a *rodeo* or an *atajo*?
